verdicts.quote: An authorised user finds a tab "Grok Bot" in Lightning Experience (App Launcher, and the direct path `/lightning/n/Grok_Bot`...) and sees the chat component.
The controller reads and writes **no** Salesforce records, so sharing, object CRUD and FLS have no data to protect; ... **sharing**: class is `with sharing`
**object CRUD**: n/a (no object touched); **FLS**: n/a (no field touched)
Users who may use the bot are whoever an admin assigns the permission set `Grok_Bot_User`. No other sharing model is added.
verdicts.missing: Who may administer the bot (edit Grok_Bot_Config, view logs) is just 'admins'. No permission set or other permission is named for administering it.

verdicts.quote: LWC component memory in the user's browser tab (R-3, R-5) | that user only ... Logged: only metadata per request ... never message text or the key.
No DML may precede a callout in the same transaction ... The controller performs no DML at all (R-9), so the rule cannot be hit.
verdicts.missing: The trigger-context restriction is never stated, and the spec picks a synchronous imperative callout, rejecting Queueable/async, so the asynchronous design the nuance requires is not adopted.

verdicts.quote: The API key is held by the platform (External Credential; Named Credential `Grok_API`...). The key is never in source, custom metadata, custom settings, the browser, or logs
at most 100 callouts ... A single callout timeout is 1 ms to 120,000 ms ... Synchronous Apex heap is 6 MB (asynchronous 12 MB); sync CPU 10 s.
Callouts ... are not made in Apex tests; tests must use `Test.setMock`.
Callouts need an endpoint registered in the org (Named Credential or Remote Site)
The controller makes the one callout and returns a small result object ... Platform Events or Queueable (async adds no value without streaming, A-6).
verdicts.missing: The interface gets the answer only as the inline return of a synchronous Apex call. No platform event, polled status or message-service notification is designed.

verdicts.quote: server-side the controller does not de-duplicate (a crafted double call makes two callouts; the only guard is the UI and the per-user permission set)
verdicts.missing: No idempotency key on the request or message. Duplicate replies are guarded only on the client side, and server-side de-duplication is deliberately left out.

verdicts.quote: Concurrent users and request volume are not specified ... synchronous call; no job, queue or polling
verdicts.missing: No concurrent-request or queue-depth limit is named, and nothing says what happens to a request the platform cannot accept.

verdicts.quote: `TIMEOUT` ... "Grok took too long to answer. Try again." | `UPSTREAM` | xAI 5xx ... | `BLOCKED` | xAI 4xx other than 401/403/429 ... "That request couldn't be processed."
`RATE_LIMIT` | xAI 429 | "Grok is busy right now. Try again in a moment." ... No automatic retry of a failed Grok call ... The user retries by hand.
Reply with `finish_reason` meaning length-truncated: the reply is shown and marked "(reply was cut off)".

Stored in the org: none (A-3): no transcript object, no DML (P-9). Logged: only metadata per request (timestamp, user Id, category, HTTP status, latency ms, request/response character counts, correlation ID)
verdicts.missing: Conversations and turns are not stored as records, and nothing records the model identifier or token/usage counts.

verdicts.quote: Conversation history lives only in the browser component (memory). Nothing is stored in the org. A page refresh or navigation away ends the conversation.
Sent to xAI: system prompt, the user's typed messages, prior assistant replies (capped), and the configured model/limits; **nothing else** (no user name, email, org ID, or record data).

with `MaxHistoryMessages`=20 and a conversation of 25 completed messages plus the new one, the body contains the system prompt, the newest 20 history messages and the new message (22); the oldest 5 are dropped.
Empty or whitespace-only input cannot be sent ... Exactly 4000 chars accepted; 4001 rejected ... Designed empty state (greeting plus 3 example prompts
`Enabled__c` (checkbox, default true), `Model__c` ... (c) Each failed request writes one log line (R-9 fields) retrievable in Setup debug logs
Logged: only metadata per request (timestamp, user Id, ...), never message text ... durable audit is **not** provided
verdicts.missing: Who asked is logged, but what was asked and answered is not. There is no durable audit record, and retention is left to platform debug-log retention.

verdicts.quote: The bot deploys only to the user-authorised development org alias ... Deploys to production-type orgs require Apex test coverage (75% org-wide, per-deploy rule)
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ between environments (dev vs sandbox vs production), and whether the target is a scratch org or a sandbox.

verdicts.quote: Hard bound: a reply wait never exceeds `TimeoutSeconds` (default 60 s, ≤120 s, P-2). The UI shows the pending state **before** the network call returns
Designed empty state (greeting plus 3 example prompts ...), loading ("Grok is thinking" with an animated indicator), error (R-6 messages inline with retry) and disabled/not-configured states.

verdicts.where: R-12; A-9; State and data assessment
verdicts.quote: Deploy adds metadata only and changes no existing org component (R-13). ... org record data identical before and after any conversation
